about.en:
Dalhousie University in Halifax, Nova Scotia, runs a single General Entrance Award (GEA) application through which first-year students, domestic and international alike, are considered for its entrance scholarships. Alongside general merit awards, several named awards target international students, such as the Sankofa Scholarship (CA$48,000 over four years for a student of African descent from the Caribbean), the Murray Family Jamaican Engineering Scholarship (CA$88,000) and a CA$15,000 commerce award for students from India.

You must be coming straight from high school (or a mature student with no transferable post-secondary study), start in the fall term and usually have an 80% average or 26 predicted IB points. You complete the GEA form in the admission portal and upload first-semester Grade 12 marks; results are sent in spring 2027.

Named awards up to CA$88,000 for some nationalities
Deadline 15 February 2027

eligibility.en: Domestic and international students entering a first undergraduate degree in fall 2027 directly from high school (or mature students without transferable study); normally 80% average or IB 26+. Some named awards are limited to certain countries (India, Jamaica, Caribbean). Open to all nationalities, including Georgia and Qatar, for the general awards.

about.en:
The Dr. Franco J. Vaccarino President's Scholarship is the University of Guelph's most prestigious entrance award for international students paying international fees. It is worth CA$42,500 over the degree and includes guaranteed on-campus residence with first-choice room preference in first year. Two awards are made each year, based on academic excellence and contributions to school and community.

Guelph, in Ontario, is known for agriculture, veterinary medicine, life sciences and environmental science. Separately, all international applicants are automatically considered for guaranteed President's International Entrance Scholarships (CA$32,500–42,500 over four years), so applying for the Vaccarino award is an extra chance at the top tier.

The University of Guelph guarantees President's International Entrance Scholarships to international fee-paying students entering a first undergraduate degree. The amount depends on your admission average: CA$10,000–20,000 in year 1 and CA$7,500 in each of years 2–4, for a total of CA$32,500–42,500.

There is no scholarship form: eligible students are told about the award in their offer of admission. To keep it, you must stay full-time and hold an 80% average each year. Guelph also offers smaller named international awards and Dean's International Scholarships.

about.en:
The International Student of Distinction (ISD) Scholarship at the University of Regina, Saskatchewan, pays for on-campus housing (and, at Tier 1, the meal plan) rather than tuition. Tier 1, for a final or early conditional high-school average of 90%+, is worth about CA$22,500 a year for four years (≈CA$90,000); Tier 2, for 85–89.99%, is about CA$11,250 a year (≈CA$45,000).

You are considered automatically if you apply directly from high school and submit all documents by the intake deadline (30 April for fall). All international undergraduate applicants with 83%+ also receive a CA$5,000 International Entrance Scholarship, and new international students get a CA$5,000-per-year bursary. Winter and spring 2027 ISD places are full, so aim for fall 2027.

All of these are automatic: your admission file is assessed and offers come with or after your admission decision. Canadian citizens and permanent residents are not eligible for the international awards.

about.en:
Kyushu University in Fukuoka, one of Japan's former imperial universities, runs four-year bachelor's programmes taught fully in English: the International Undergraduate Program in the School of Engineering, the Bioresource and Bioenvironment programme (Agriculture) and the School of Interdisciplinary Science and Innovation. Entry is in October.

From the October 2027 applicant pool, Kyushu picks a few candidates with outstanding screening results and recommends them to Japan's Ministry of Education (MEXT). Recipients get exemption from the entrance and tuition fees for four years, a monthly allowance of ¥117,000 and return airfare. The online application system is open only from 7 to 11 December 2026, after which all documents must be posted; some programmes require minimum standardized test scores (SAT, ACT, IB or A-level).

Tohoku University in Sendai, a top-5 Japanese national university, is replacing its need-based tuition exemption with a new merit scholarship for international students enrolling from the 2027 academic year. It covers either the full tuition fee or half of it and is expected to reach approximately the top one-third of admitted students, judged on entrance examination results and academic performance.

For bachelor's students the main English route is the Future Global Leadership (FGL) programme: Advanced Molecular Chemistry, International Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, and Applied Marine Biology, with October entry and applications in January. FGL applicants may also be considered for MEXT university-recommended scholarships (up to 8 places) and the President Fellowship. Tohoku says full rules will be announced on its website once finalised.

about.en:
The International Max Planck Research School (IMPRS) for Ageing (Cologne Graduate School of Ageing Research) is an English-language doctoral programme run by the Max Planck Institute for Biology of Ageing, the CECAD cluster and the University of Cologne. Doctoral researchers work on projects in biology of ageing, metabolism, genetics and age-related disease, with structured training, thesis committees and international peers.

Selected candidates receive funding for the PhD (normally an employment contract or Max Planck support contract covering salary and social insurance; no tuition is charged in Germany). The school recruits internationally; the application deadline for the 2027 intake is 3 November 2026, followed by interviews in early 2027.

Successful candidates enter the third year of a licence or the first year of a master's, study for three years and graduate with a master's degree and the ENS diploma, receiving a grant of €1,000 a month paid monthly for three years.

There are two tracks: Arts & Humanities (e.g. philosophy, history, literature, economics, political studies, linguistics, cognitive science) for candidates under 25 with three years of university study, and Sciences (biology, chemistry, earth science, computer science, mathematics, physics, cognitive science) for candidates under 26 with at least one year abroad at university.
